question: A 2200-g (4-lbs 13-oz) female newborn is delivered at term to a 37-year-old gravida 2, para 1 woman. The newborn is at the 10th percentile for length, 14th percentile for weight, and 3rd percentile for head circumference. Examination shows “punched-out“ skin lesions on the scalp, cleft lip, and a small chin. There is a convex-shaped deformity of the plantar surface of the feet. Auscultation shows a holosystolic murmur heard best at the left lower sternal border. Some of her intestines protrude through the umbilicus, covered by a thin membranous sac. An MRI of the brain shows a single ventricle and a fusion of the basal ganglia. Which of the following additional findings is most likely to be seen in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)" -> "Holosystolic murmur" -> "Ventricular septal defect" -> "Overlapping fingers" -> 80% CHAIN: "Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)" -> "Single ventricle on brain MRI" -> "Fusion of basal ganglia" -> "Hypoplastic philtrum" -> 75% CHAIN: "Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)" -> "Cleft lip" -> "Small chin" -> "Single palmar crease" -> 80%
analysis: The constellation of findings in this newborn is consistent with the diagnosis of Patau syndrome, also known as trisomy 13. The presence of cleft lip, small chin, plantar surface deformity, umbilical hernia, holosystolic murmur, and brain abnormalities such as single ventricle and basal ganglia fusion are characteristic features of this condition.
